userStories.notes: One review of all of Phase 7, four issues found and all fixed here. (1) applyEntry had no guard on state.removed, so entries already in the queue when the removal commit landed were still handed to processEntry, which throws for a client that holds no keys past its own removal -- the queue reads that as a fatal commit and overwrites the removed page's explanation with "Reload to resynchronise". (2) Nothing bound a join request's identity to its key package: the room stores both verbatim and cannot parse a key package, so a socket claiming one identity while attaching somebody else's key package had the creator commit an Add for a leaf the asker cannot open, address the Welcome to somebody who cannot read it, and record the claimant as admitted, which is what mayWriteLog reads. keyPackageBelongsTo is the check, applied in commit (throws), onPending (skips silently, because that list is re-broadcast) and the view (Approve disabled with a reason). (3) The waiting view's disclosure was false -- the request survives a closed tab, the private key that opens the Welcome does not -- so it now says both halves separately. (4) The item US-014 left here: in Phase 7 the stuck identity does have a way out, a reload makes a new signature key and therefore a new stranger, and the join-failure status now names it; the rest is Phase 8's, since persistence is what removes that escape.
